text:
Columbus arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 2-1 shootout win over Dallas in which the Blue Jackets trailed in the third period. They're 3-2-0 in their last five. Buffalo's three-game winning streak ended with a 2-1 home loss to Ottawa two days ago, and the Sabres are playing without Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk. They also met on Oct 1, when Columbus won 6-3.

Neither team has been dominant at five on five. Columbus has taken 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, Buffalo 50%, and our model projects 3.27 goals for Buffalo and 2.89 for Columbus. Buffalo's penalty habit, 4.1 minors a game, keeps handing the other side power plays. The projected goalies are Jet Greaves for Columbus and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen for Buffalo. Both sit below expectation this season in goals saved above expected (a measure of saves beyond what the shots deserved): Greaves at -0.85, Luukkonen at -2.24. Last year both were strongly positive, at 15.02 and 9.12.

Tage Thompson is our top Buffalo scorer at 41% to score, on a four-game point streak, and Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report posted that he "stays blazing hot." For Columbus, Zach Werenski is 68% for a point, and Mathieu Olivier is one goal from 50 in his career. Our under-the-radar picks are Buffalo's Jason Zucker, a fourth-liner with 2.3 expected goals in his last six games (22% to score), and Jack Quinn, 65% for a point because his line creates chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
